price.server_offset_source: empirical weekly offset from the M5 daily break (UTC+2 on EST, UTC+3 on EDT)
price.usage: Use mid as the gold price. Its age = brief time - quote_utc; if over 15 minutes, state the age. Fall back to a web spot price only if this file is stale (generated_utc more than 60 minutes old, or quote_utc more than 60 minutes old on a weekday market session) or the run failed (file missing or unreadable), and say which source the brief used.

driver_notes: dollar driver = ICE DXY formula rebuilt from Vantage MT5 D1 closes of EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, USDCAD, USDSEK, USDCHF (17:00 New York close, same feed as gold). FRED DTWEXBGS kept only for the old-vs-new comparison.

server_offset.method: CME daily maintenance break start (17:00 New York) per Mon-Thu; cross-checked against Sunday 18:00 New York open
server_offset.note: Vantage server time = UTC+2 while New York is on EST and UTC+3 while on EDT (offsets seen in sample: [2, 3]); server midnight = 17:00 New York. D1 bars therefore close at 17:00 New York, near the FRED yield/oil/USD daily observation times.

q1_normalised_excursions.definition: Ruler = the published expected range: the walk-forward implied-vol range (GVZ, intraday variance share and calibration constant from the trailing 250 sessions) x the tier-1 release ratio on tier-1 days; the calibrated 20-day E when implied vol is unavailable (scale_used). Each session uses its own ruler; up = (high - open)/ruler, down = (open - low)/ruler; P(touch k) = share of sessions with excursion >= k rulers

q1_shadow_calibrated_E.definition: E = calibrated expected range: the mean (high - low, $) of the same window over its previous 20 complete sessions (E_raw) x k, k = median(range / E_raw) over the 250 sessions before, so 1 E is the typical (median) range. Each session uses its own E; up = (high - open)/E, down = (open - low)/E; P(touch k) = share of sessions with excursion >= k*E

q2_us_window_by_release.definition: release = tier <= 2 release inside 13:00-20:00 UK; jobless claims excluded

q2b_us_window_by_release_tier.collapse_rule: tiers 1 and 2 are merged if tier 1 has fewer than 30 sessions

q4_driver_regression.usage: Context only. Never multiply a session's dollar move by these betas to state a gold amount; see dollar.usage.

overnight.definition: last daily reopen (after the 1-hour break) -> 08:00 London

london_morning.definition: 08:00 -> 13:00 London; the US window's reference range

reference_levels.distance_note: distance_scale = (level - latest price) / the window's ruler (scale_usd, the published expected range); every E-named rule below is in rulers. distance_E and p_reach_E are the shadow calibrated 20-day E. The excursion arrays are measured from the window OPEN, so p_reach_from_array is exact only when the latest price is the window open; before the open it is an approximation. Levels within 0.1 rulers are 'at price' and carry no published percentage.
reference_levels.partial_note: partial=true means the level's window was still forming; computed_to_london is the close time of the last bar included (e.g. 'morning range as at 12:45').
reference_levels.confluence_note: Within 0.15 rulers of a level, own entry included, over every candidate before dedup. confluence_sources (primary) = independent price events: labels printed by the same M5 bar are one source, a reaction level and the turns it was built from are one source, each round number and moving average is its own source. confluence_labels (secondary) = distinct level types. Neither is used in any probability. backed_by = the independent-source count, then each source's labels in short form (same-source labels joined by '/', round numbers as the price).

dollar.index: MT5-built dollar index (ICE DXY formula on Vantage EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, USDCAD, USDSEK, USDCHF)
dollar.line: Dollar index 102.16, +0.01 (+0.01%) on the day. Over the last 250 days gold has tended to move the opposite way to the dollar, but loosely: the dollar accounts for about 19% of gold's day-to-day movement. Context only, not a guide to today's gold move.
dollar.usage: Publish the dollar index level and its change, and the relationship as context only. Never convert the dollar's move into a gold figure: no per-session dollar amount for gold (for example 'worth about $0.40 of gold'). The 250-day relationship is an average and does not apply to one session.

range_adjust.definition: Pre-session range = log(high/low) over the window before each session (UK: London 23:00-08:00, New York 08:00-13:00), for gold and for the dollar index (5-minute bars), divided by the same window's mean over the previous 20 sessions. Busy = ratio >= 1.20. adjusted_usd = the published expected range (forecast_usd) x the state multiplier; adjusted_low/high = session open -/+ half of it, rounded to $1. Past rates are fixed figures from the study.

oil_regime.definition: Last 120 trading days of hourly bars (close to close, consecutive hours only, the forming hour excluded): share of hours where gold and USOUSD both moved and moved in opposite directions. 'against gold' >= 55%, 'with gold' <= 45%, otherwise 'mixed'.

direction_lean.definition: Pre-session move = log(close/open) over the window before each session (UK: London 23:00-08:00, New York 08:00-13:00). Hard up / hard down = top / bottom 10% of the previous 250 sessions' moves; dollar and oil both down / up = each in its bottom / top 25%. For each signal, the past sessions where it was active: share where gold closed the session above its open (close_up) and share where gold rose further from the open than it fell (ext_up), raw, weighted by recency (weight = 0.5^(age_days/182)) and over the last 12 months. Signals are listed separately; there is no combined score. Past frequencies - not a forecast and not a trade call.
